item.text: The bug is clear: `"active" in row["status"]` is a substring check, so an account whose status is `inactive` still contains the word "active" and gets counted in the active total (the same would apply to a status like `reactivated`, which `test_exact_status` guards). The fix is an exact status comparison.
item.reasoning: The bug: `"active" in row["status"]` matches "inactive" and "reactivated". Test test_exact_status expects "reactivated" to be excluded. Fix: `row["status"] == "active"` — perhaps case-insensitive? Keep small: exact match. Maybe strip whitespace? Keep simple: `row["status"].strip() == "active"`? Tests pass either way. I'll do `== "active"` (exact). Run tests.
